A run is 5 seeds x 5 diffusion samples, so 25 predictions, for every variant
except ESMFold2, which produces 5. Comparing per run therefore flatters
ESMFold2. The per-prediction column is the fair comparison.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../bin")
from _analysis_common import *

d = load()
rt = d["rt"]
```

## Runtime against memory

```{python}
med = (rt.groupby(["model", "msa"])
         .agg(runtime=("elapsed_min", "median"), memory=("peak_rss_gb", "median"))
         .reset_index())

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.4, 6.4))
for flag, col, lab, z in [("no_msa", NO_MSA_COLOR, "No MSA", 4),
                          ("msa", MSA_COLOR, "MSA", 3)]:
    sub = med[med["msa"] == flag]
    ax.scatter(sub["runtime"], sub["memory"], s=90, color=col, alpha=0.65,
               edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6, label=lab, zorder=z)

LABEL_LEFT = {("af2m", "msa"), ("esmfold2", "no_msa"), ("boltz1", "no_msa"),
              ("boltz2", "no_msa"), ("colabfold", "no_msa")}
for _, r in med.iterrows():
    key = (r["model"], r["msa"])
    name = DISPLAY.get(r["model"], r["model"])
    left = key in LABEL_LEFT
    ax.annotate(name, (r["runtime"], r["memory"]), fontsize=7.5,
                xytext=(-8 if left else 8, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                ha="right" if left else "left", va="center", zorder=5)
ax.set_xscale("log")
readable_log(ax.xaxis, TIME_TICKS)
ax.set_xlabel("Median wall-clock per run (minutes, log scale)")
ax.set_ylabel("Median peak resident memory (GB)")
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5), frameon=True, fontsize=10)
save_fig(fig, "runtime_vs_peak_memory")
plt.show()
```

## Cost table

```{python}
N_PREDICTIONS = {"esmfold2": 5}      # every other variant runs 5 seeds x 5 samples
cost = (rt.groupby(["model", "msa"])
          .agg(n_targets=("elapsed_min", "size"),
               mean_min=("elapsed_min", "mean"),
               median_min=("elapsed_min", "median"),
               min_min=("elapsed_min", "min"),
               max_min=("elapsed_min", "max"),
               mean_peak_rss_gb=("peak_rss_gb", "mean"))
          .reset_index())
cost["predictions"] = cost["model"].map(lambda m: N_PREDICTIONS.get(m, 25))
cost["min_per_prediction"] = cost["mean_min"] / cost["predictions"]
cost["combo"] = [combo_label(m, f) for m, f in zip(cost["model"], cost["msa"])]
cost[["combo", "n_targets", "mean_min", "median_min", "min_min", "max_min",
      "predictions", "min_per_prediction", "mean_peak_rss_gb"]].round(2) \
    .sort_values("min_per_prediction").reset_index(drop=True)
```

- Cost spans two orders of magnitude. AlphaFold3 without an MSA is cheapest at
  under two minutes. AlphaFold2-Multimer takes about two hours, almost all of it
  in its own MSA search.
- Per prediction, Boltz-2 costs roughly a quarter of ESMFold2 and a third of its
  peak memory, despite the two looking comparable per run. Boltz-2 also varies
  by seconds across targets where ESMFold2 varies by minutes.
- Memory does not track runtime. ColabFold is among the slowest but the
  lightest, and ESMFold2 is fast per run but the heaviest after
  AlphaFold2-Multimer.

## Throughput under a fixed memory budget

How many predictions could a host with a given amount of RAM produce in one
hour, assuming GPUs are not the constraint?

```{python}
MEM_GB = 1000.0
tp = med.merge(cost[["model", "msa", "predictions"]], on=["model", "msa"])
tp = tp[tp["msa"] == "no_msa"].copy()
tp["parallel"] = np.floor(MEM_GB / tp["memory"]).astype(int)
tp["runs_per_hour"] = 60.0 / tp["runtime"]
tp["predictions_per_hour"] = (tp["parallel"] * tp["runs_per_hour"]
                              * tp["predictions"]).round(0).astype(int)
tp["model"] = tp["model"].map(lambda m: DISPLAY.get(m, m))
tp[["model", "runtime", "memory", "parallel", "runs_per_hour", "predictions",
    "predictions_per_hour"]].round(2).sort_values("predictions_per_hour",
                                                  ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
```

- Under a memory cap the ranking changes again. ESMFold2 pays twice, being the
  heaviest model so fewest instances fit, and returning 5 predictions per run
  rather than 25.
- Boltz-2 delivers several times the sampling per unit wall-clock at a third of
  the memory, which is the practical case for using it in a no-MSA design
  setting. It costs some accuracy against AlphaFold3 without an MSA.

Caveats. `peak_rss_gb` is host RAM rather than GPU memory, and VRAM is usually
the binding constraint in practice. The throughput table assumes perfect
parallelism with no I/O contention. Queueing time is excluded, so these are
execution times rather than time-to-result on a busy cluster. Runtimes cover 17
of the 18 targets, since one run has no usable trace row.
